name: rates-bonds/cef-discount-reversion
title: CEF discount reversion — dollar-neutral long/short of bond closed-end funds on discount-to-NAV dislocations
description: A closed-end fund has no creation/redemption, so retail flow pushes its price away from NAV for days. Long funds whose ln(close/NAV) is >= 2.5 % below its own 60-session mean relative to the muni/taxable group median, short the reverse, each held until the gap closes; 5 % per name on the smaller side, the other side scaled to match (net 0, gross <= 1.0); entered one session after the signal because the NAV is published in the evening.
symbol: US bond closed-end funds (snapshot universe, ~170 legs, ~16-34 held)
direction: long/short, dollar-neutral (net 0 by construction), gross avg 0.60 / max 1.00

backtest.cost_type: 10 bp per side all-in on every trade (sum|dw| at the entry close); no borrow fee, no financing

live_notes: SIM book: every leg fills at the panel's daily close (fee 10 bp, slippage 0 = the research's 10 bp/side all-in). No order book, no closing auction, no rejection or partial fill. Much weaker evidence than a venue fill -- and the fill cost is the report's own main uncertainty: range-based estimators put the half-spread of these funds at 12-15 bp, and the OOS Sharpe is 1.71 at 20 bp, 0.91 at 30 bp, break-even ~41 bp.

NO BORROW MODEL: the book shorts closed-end funds freely and at no fee. CEF borrow is often scarce. Report: 300 bp/yr borrow -> 2.51 IS / 2.15 OOS; the long leg against the equal-weight liquid universe is 1.70 OOS; the long leg unhedged is 0.89 with CEF beta.

Distributions are not credited: legs are marked at the last (ex-distribution) close, as every yahoo-daily sim book is, while the backtest took total returns from adjusted closes. Bond CEFs distribute ~monthly, so the long side under-earns and the short side over-earns by its yield; the book is dollar-neutral, so the live track differs from the backtest by the long-minus-short yield gap on ~0.3 of capital per side. Read small live P&L differences with that in mind.
Capacity: the report puts real capacity at roughly $1-3M (5 % positions in ~$1M-a-day funds). Irrelevant at a $2,500 sim ticket; decisive for anything real.
Regime: the return is paid in stress (2008-09, 2020, 2022). 2015-2019 was 1.23 at 10 bp and 0.46 at 20 bp; 2018 lost 0.4 %. A flat first year is within the backtest.

Data: once per session (outside 09:00-17:00 New York) the runner rebuilds data/CEF_BOND_panel_d.parquet with the research fetcher fetch_cef.build_panel() (yfinance prices + X<T>X NAV tickers, ~1-2 min; this is the same file research reads) and feeds the full history to strategy.target_weights. yfinance logs ~10 'possibly delisted' NAV tickers on every rebuild: those are the 10 snapshot funds with no NAV series, absent from the backtest too.

Bar: NOT min-over-legs. The bar advances to the latest session on which >= 150 funds printed a close (170 at deploy) AND >= 95 % of them have a NAV on the previous (signal) session; until then the daemon re-checks every 30 min. Both thresholds are runner guards, not research parameters: a NAV Yahoo has not posted reads as 'no discount' and would flatten that fund's position. If funds merge/liquidate until fewer than 150 print, the book stops advancing loudly -- refresh cef_universe.csv (fetch_cef.py --universe) through research.

Universe: the committed cef_universe.csv snapshot (funds alive 2026-10). `symbols` lists the 168 funds with a price history of >= 250 sessions at deploy (DHY excluded by the strategy; FSSL has 227 sessions and a mirrored NAV, so it cannot be eligible). open_universe=True: a ledger written under an older list resumes instead of restarting.

Survivorship and selection (from the report): survivors-only universe (estimated cost < 0.75 %/yr, not measured); 188 configurations scored, the threshold family designed after the rank family's OOS cost ladder had been seen, parameters chosen on IS at a 20 bp stress cost.

Flatten: the dashboard's flatten rebuilds the book via broker_from_meta with YahooQuotes over 168 per-ticker caches (data/<T>_d.parquet, 1 h cache); it may re-download every leg and hit its timeout, in which case it fails without writing anything.

Deploy check 2026-10-10: runner --check on bar 2026-10-09 = 21 long at +0.0238 / 13 short at -0.0385, gross 1.000, net 0.000. Matches strategy.target_weights and the PR's 07_weights.parquet row 2026-10-09 exactly (max|diff| 0), also after a fresh build_panel() rebuild. Lag test against 07_weights.parquet over 2003-2026: lag 0 max|diff| 0.0; lag 1 and 2 max|diff| 0.10 -- the file is unshifted, row t is the weight held close t -> close t+1.
